subject: Chemistry
b6_reason: The carbonate ion has three equivalent canonical forms (the double bond delocalised over the three C-O bonds); the other three statements are false.
b6_working: Option 1: ozone has two resonance structures, not three. Option 2: BF3 is trigonal planar and symmetric, so its dipole moment is zero. Option 3: in NF3 the N-F bond dipoles oppose the lone-pair moment, so NF3 (0.24 D) is much less polar than NH3 (1.46 D). Option 4: CO3 2- has three equivalent canonical forms - correct.
b6_note: Option 4's formula is damaged in the source ('2 3CO -' plus an explicit '[unreadable notation]' marker); it is read as the carbonate ion CO3 2-, which the rest of the option supports, but the rendering is broken.
